nodes.label: Prose journeys as the source of executable specs
nodes.rationale: The same journey exists four times (web, Android, iOS, desktop). Written directly as code each implementation quietly becomes its own slightly different story and nobody can tell whether the Android suite and the Playwright suite test the same thing. One prose source keeps them honest and is the artifact an agent can be handed.

nodes.label: Shared test ids (src/shared/test-ids.ts) with parity test
nodes.rationale: Every journey step names elements by shared id rather than a platform-specific tag, and tests/test-ids-parity.test.ts fails the build if the ids drift apart across languages.

nodes.label: Four agent lanes: author, healer, explorer, screenshot triage
nodes.rationale: A: agent authors a spec from a journey file, but it must pass three clean consecutive replays with no agent involved before commit. B: agent proposes a selector fix from a trace or captured device state — a human merges, never auto-merged. C: nightly free-roam explorer, findings filed only once a deterministic replay reproduces them; this is where agents genuinely beat scripted tests. D: an LLM only sorts screenshot diffs to cut review noise, never decides the gate.

nodes.label: CI never calls a model
nodes.rationale: Nondeterministic action selection, model-version drift changing behaviour underneath you, minutes of latency per run, and — specific to this product — a prompt-injection surface, because the app renders untrusted agent output and an LLM driving that UI is a live target. A gate that is 90% reliable is worse than no gate: people learn to re-run it instead of reading it. Agents are good at writing the script and bad at being the gate.

hyperedges.label: Journey-driven verification: prose specs, shared ids, and the CI lanes that run them
